result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A has a clean rise-and-fall curve with stage labels and a shaded mix window drawn on the chart. Its times are framed as rough and temperature-dependent, but its 'Why the timing matters' box is cut off below the fold. B's jar sequence is a nice idea, but the descriptions under the jars overlap and can't be read, and the 'now sunken' label sits away from its marker. Those are clear rendering defects, even though B fits on one screen and states the mixing advice clearly. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A has a clear jar-sequence idea with good approximate-time framing, but the description text under the jars overlaps and is unreadable, and the 'now sunken' label floats loosely away from the jar it refers to. B renders cleanly: a rise-and-fall curve with Feed/Rise/Peak/Collapse and a shaded mix window labelled right on the chart, times explicitly tied to a warm kitchen and called rough. Its one weakness is that the 'Why the timing matters' box runs below the first screen.
